catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extraction from Continuous Architecture System (CAS) CLI Runner codebase, focusing on agent boundaries, orchestration, governance, evaluation, and knowledge persistence.
analysis_limits: Only symbols provided in key_files used; no full file contents inspected.
Agent definitions limited to verifier subagent and skill directories; other agents may exist but unverified.
No runtime execution observed; patterns inferred from code structure and names.

system_map.overview: The CAS system is a CLI-driven orchestrator that coordinates agents and governance mechanisms to continuously evolve an architecture knowledge base. It uses a centralised FlowRunner to execute flows, a governance layer with typed models and state machines to control changes, and a persistent knowledge repository (cas-knowledge) for shared memory.

agents.name: Verifier Agent
agents.role: Verifies agent outputs and architecture artifacts before acceptance, acting as a quality gate.

agents.name: Skill Agents (implicit)
agents.role: Perform specialised tasks such as adding features, generating drawio diagrams, refactoring knowledge links, and syncing governance reviews.

orchestration.description: FlowRunner in src/cas_runner/runner.py drives sequential execution of steps, while governance engines (action and compliance) enforce constraints. Skills are invoked as atomic units within flows.

tools_and_integrations.name: LiteLLM
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Unified LLM access with provider abstraction for production use.

tools_and_integrations.name: MockLLM
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Deterministic LLM simulation for reproducible tests and evaluations.

tools_and_integrations.name: OpenTelemetry
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Observability and tracing of agent execution and governance actions.

tools_and_integrations.name: GitHub Actions Workflows
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Automate validation, build, steering sync, and skill evals.

state_and_memory.description: cas-knowledge repository stores global patterns, rules, signals, governance decisions, and runtime traces.
Pydantic models define governance state (inventory, health, risks, findings) for structured processing.
Governance health is calculated from underlying metrics to provide an at-a-glance status.

patterns.name: LLM Provider Abstraction via Client Interface

tool_protocols.notes: Abstracts LLM access; no native tool protocol used in this pattern.

optimisation_targets.notes: Abstraction enables swapping providers without changing agent logic.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Prefer simple client interface over framework-specific complexity.

patterns.summary: Agents access LLMs through a common client interface, with LiteLLMClient for production and MockLLMClient for tests.
patterns.intent: Decouple agent logic from specific LLM vendor and enable deterministic testing.
patterns.context: Both clients live in src/cas_runner/llm/ and are likely injected via the runner or service layer.
patterns.solution: Define a common client interface; LiteLLMClient wraps litellm for real calls, MockLLMClient returns scripted responses.
implementation_signals: Two client classes in same package

failure_modes: Mock not representing real LLM behaviour

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt in any agent system needing provider portability or test determinism; ensure interface is minimal and stable.

patterns.name: Typed Governance State Contracts

tool_protocols.notes: State is structured via Pydantic models, not external tool protocols.

optimisation_targets.notes: Typed models catch state errors early.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Schema-first approach reduces ambiguity in agent-produced state.

patterns.summary: Governance state (inventory, health, risks, findings) is modelled with Pydantic types to enforce validation and consistency.
patterns.intent: Ensure agent-written governance data conforms to a schema, preventing malformed state.
patterns.context: All governance data structures are defined in models.py and used by compliance and action engines.
patterns.solution: Define all governance entities as Pydantic models; validate on creation and serialization.

failure_modes: Schema migrations needed as governance changes

patterns.reuse_notes: Use in any system where agents produce or consume shared state; keep schemas explicit and versioned.

patterns.name: Governance State Machine with Transition Registry

tool_protocols.notes: State transitions are defined in code, not via external tools.

optimisation_targets.notes: State machine limits invalid governance actions.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Explicit transitions make control flow predictable.

patterns.summary: GovernanceActionEngine and TransitionRegistry define allowed state transitions for governance actions, ensuring controlled progression.
patterns.intent: Prevent invalid or irreversible governance state changes by agents.
patterns.context: GovernanceActionEngine uses TransitionRegistry to validate and execute moves between governance states.
patterns.solution: Centralise legal transitions in a registry; engine checks each action against it before applying.

evidence.note: State transition definitions and execution engine.

costs: May restrict legitimate actions if incomplete

patterns.reuse_notes: Reuse for any stateful agent workflow needing explicit legal moves; keep registry separate from engine for testability.

patterns.name: Compliance Validation Guardrail

tool_protocols.notes: Guardrail is a code-level validation rather than external tool.

optimisation_targets.notes: Compliance checks aim to prevent non-conforming outputs.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Use deterministic validation over autonomy to ensure safety.

patterns.summary: ComplianceEngine checks agent outputs or actions against predefined rules and produces ComplianceFindings for rejection or remediation.
patterns.intent: Enforce constraints on agent behaviour before allowing changes to propagate.
patterns.context: Used within governance flow after actions are generated, before state transitions.
patterns.solution: Implement an engine that takes proposed changes or outputs, checks against rules, and returns structured findings.
patterns.reuse_notes: Adapt to any agent pipeline where outputs must be validated before acceptance; keep rules declarative.

patterns.name: Cross-Framework Agent Context Merging

tool_protocols.notes: Merges configuration files, not tool protocol.

optimisation_targets.notes: Unified context reduces misconfiguration across frameworks.

patterns.summary: AgenticMerger combines governance blocks and Claude settings into a unified agent context, ensuring consistent rules across platforms.
patterns.intent: Unify agent instructions and governance from multiple sources to avoid drift and conflicting rules.
patterns.context: Used during workspace bootstrap to merge CAS governance block and Claude settings.
patterns.solution: Provide a merger that programmatically combines relevant YAML/markdown blocks, with precedence rules.

failure_modes: One platform's config overwrites another inadvertently

patterns.reuse_notes: Use in multi-framework agent setups; define explicit precedence and test merge outputs.

patterns.name: Flow-Based Sequential Execution with Shared Context

optimisation_targets.notes: Sequential context passing reduces concurrency-related errors.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Explicit linear flow is easier to debug and validate.

patterns.summary: FlowRunner executes a sequence of steps, mutating a shared context that is passed to each subsequent step.
patterns.intent: Structure multi-step agent workflows in a deterministic, traceable order.
patterns.context: FlowRunner is the central executor in CAS, likely invoked by CLI.
patterns.solution: Define a runner that iterates over a list of steps, passing a context object and collecting results.
patterns.reuse_notes: Reuse for any deterministic pipeline; consider checkpointing state for fault tolerance.

patterns.name: Evaluatable Skill Suite with Assertions

tool_protocols.notes: Skills are evaluated via assertions, not MCP.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Allows skill autonomy while providing structured evaluation.

patterns.summary: Skills are defined alongside testable eval cases with assertions, allowing automated evaluation of skill correctness.
patterns.intent: Make agent skills verifiable and improve reliability through automated evals.
patterns.context: Skill suite models (SkillEvalSuite, SkillEvalCase, SkillAssertions) support evaluating skills in CI.
patterns.solution: Define evaluation models that pair each skill with cases and assertions; run in dedicated workflow.

costs: Potential false confidence if cases insufficient

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt for any agent skill/tool system; keep eval cases close to skill definitions.

patterns.name: Dedicated Verifier Agent

tool_protocols.notes: Agent defined as markdown config for Claude, likely invoked as subagent.

optimisation_targets.notes: Separation of duties to catch errors.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Autonomous production steps, but verification is a dedicated role.

patterns.summary: A separate verifier subagent reviews outputs or architecture artefacts before finalisation, providing an independent quality gate.
patterns.intent: Add an independent check on agent outputs to reduce errors and ensure compliance.
patterns.context: Verifier agent definition exists for both Claude and generic agents, suggesting it is called at the end of workflows.
patterns.solution: Define a subagent with explicit verification instructions and integrate it as a step before final acceptance.

failure_modes: Verifier not integrated into all flows

patterns.reuse_notes: Reuse in any multi-agent pipeline where a validation step is needed; define clear success criteria.

patterns.name: Persistent Knowledge Blackboard

tool_protocols.notes: Shared knowledge repository serves as inter-agent memory.

optimisation_targets.notes: Reuse of historical knowledge improves decisions.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Agents can read/write shared memory to collaborate.

patterns.summary: A persistent directory (cas-knowledge) stores global patterns, rules, signals, decisions, and traces, acting as a shared blackboard for agents.
patterns.intent: Enable agents to access and contribute to a durable institutional memory across projects.
patterns.context: CAS uses cas-knowledge as central repository for architecture knowledge, governance, and runtime traces.
patterns.solution: Maintain a structured directory with subdirectories for patterns, rules, signals, decisions, and traces; agents read/write as needed.
patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt for any multi-agent system needing durable shared memory; enforce directory conventions.

patterns.name: Template-Driven Knowledge Capture

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Templates guide agents to produce consistent artefacts.

patterns.summary: Architecture knowledge artefacts (ADRs, patterns, experiments) are created from predefined templates, ensuring consistent structure.
patterns.intent: Standardise knowledge capture to make artefacts machine-readable and comparable.
patterns.context: cas-knowledge/templates contains templates for ADRs, pattern, experiment, heuristic, etc.
patterns.solution: Provide markdown templates with required sections; agents are instructed to fill them.

failure_modes: Templates not updated with evolving needs

patterns.reuse_notes: Use templates for any agent-produced knowledge; version templates to keep consistency.

patterns.name: Evidence-to-Pattern Promotion

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Promotes learning while keeping governance control.

patterns.summary: Validated heuristics are promoted to patterns through a formal process using experiment and promotion templates.
patterns.intent: Systematically evolve ad-hoc heuristics into vetted architectural patterns.
patterns.context: Templates exist for experiments, heuristic-to-pattern conversion, and promotion decisions.
patterns.solution: Require evidence from experiments and a promotion decision template before escalating a heuristic to a pattern.
patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt in knowledge-centric agent systems to mature heuristics into patterns.

patterns.name: Mock LLM for Deterministic Evaluation
patterns.summary: MockLLMClient provides deterministic LLM responses, enabling reproducible tests and evaluations of agent flows.
patterns.intent: Remove LLM variability from test and eval suites.
patterns.context: Complements LiteLLMClient in the same package for use in unit tests and CI.
forces: Cost of real calls in CI
patterns.solution: Implement a mock that returns scripted responses based on input, following the same client interface.

costs: Mock may diverge from real behaviour
Test coverage for provider-specific features lost
failure_modes: Tests pass but real LLM fails

patterns.reuse_notes: Use alongside provider abstraction; keep mock scenarios representative of real usage.

patterns.name: Governance Health Monitoring

tool_protocols.notes: Health is computed locally, not via external tool.

patterns.summary: Governance health is computed from metrics and presented with explanatory reasons, giving a status overview of the governance system.
patterns.intent: Provide a quick, explainable health check for governance processes.
patterns.context: Dashboard health_model calculates HealthStatus and reasons based on governance data.
patterns.solution: Define HealthStatus enum and a calculation function that returns health plus reasons.

failure_modes: Metrics not updated lead to false health

patterns.reuse_notes: Reuse pattern for any system needing explainable health metrics.

patterns.name: Workspace Bootstrapping with Governance Injection

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures agents start with correct context.

patterns.summary: Workspace initialization injects governance blocks, symlinks skills, and renders onboarding checklists to prepare agent environments.
patterns.intent: Automate agent workspace setup to ensure governance and skills are consistently available.
patterns.context: bootstrap.py provides functions to merge governance block, set up Claude settings, and symlink skills.
patterns.solution: Provide a bootstrap script that performs file operations (merge, symlink, render) and prints a checklist.

costs: Potential for broken symlinks on some OS

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt for agent environments needing reproducible setup; ensure idempotence.

anti_patterns.name: Agent Configuration Duplication Across Frameworks
symptoms: Same agent/skill definitions repeated in .agents and .claude directories
Manual changes may not propagate to all copies
impact: Configuration drift leads to inconsistent agent behaviour
Governance rules may diverge between platforms
suggested_remediation: Generate copies from a single source of truth during bootstrap
Add validation to detect drift across duplicated files
Use symlinks or includes where possible

anti_patterns.name: Unbounded Growth of Shared Knowledge Repository
symptoms: Large number of pattern, rule, signal, and trace files without evident lifecycle management
No explicit retention policy observed in code

where_observed.note: Global knowledge directories without curation signals.

impact: Governance decisions based on outdated patterns
suggested_remediation: Implement retention policies or archival process
Add quality gates for new knowledge entries
Use metadata (e.g., last-reviewed date) to identify stale entries

anti_patterns.name: Mock LLM Divergence from Real Behaviour
symptoms: Tests pass against mock but fail in production
Mock responses become outdated as LLM prompts evolve

where_observed.note: Mock implementation may not reflect current LLM capabilities.

impact: Production failures not caught by CI
suggested_remediation: Periodically refresh mock scenarios from real LLM outputs
Include contract tests against a real LLM in non-CI environments
